optionalSupplies: A quiet chew your dog already knows
substitutes: No rubber mat? A yoga mat.
No scent cloths? Rub a clean T-shirt on their bed.
title: The Waymarked Walk
clue: The path was built for a dog who knows the world by feel and smell, and every turn has its own marker.
reveal: A short indoor or yard path for a dog who sees or hears less, or who is older or unsure on new ground: two textures underfoot and a familiar smell at each marker, so they can read the route with paws and nose and arrive confidently.
objective: Build a short waymarked route of two textures and scents, walk it together once, and let your dog use it as they choose.
instructions: Pick a short route (a hallway, one room, or a straight stretch of fully secure yard) with no steps, no furniture corners and no slippery floors. Keep the layout the same from now on: no moving furniture.

Lay two waymarks on a non-slip underlay: a rubber mat at the start and a rug at the destination. At each, place a different mild home scent: a corner of your worn T-shirt, their blanket or a clean cloth from their favorite spot.
Before the walk, make sure they know you are there: stay where they can see or smell you, offer your hand to sniff, and never touch a sleeping or unaware dog from behind or startle them.
Walk the route once together on a loose leash or alongside, speaking softly, pausing at each waymark while they sniff. Do not steer; they can repeat any section or stop.
At the end, a comfy bed and a quiet chew are waiting. Let them settle with no cues.
Leave the waymarks in place as their 'lighthouses'. If they seem to enjoy it, add one new waymark a week, and change nothing else in the route.
twist: The route is built from the dog's strengths, touch and smell, so a dog who sees or hears less, or who is less sure of the world, reads it with confidence.
variations: Easiest: one waymark and a bed, just a few steps long.
Yard version: paving, turf and a mat in a secure yard on a calm day.
After a week, add a third waymark that smells of a favorite place or person, and keep the rest unchanged.
Seated owner: lay the route and sit at the end; the dog walks it to you.
completion: Your dog has met the route and walked or sniffed some of it; counts even if they stop, return or go to bed.
photoIdea: Their nose resting on the rug at the end, or the line of waymarks seen from the doorway.
memoryPrompt: Which waymark did your dog spend longest on, and how did they seem on the way back?
supplies: Worn T-shirt, blanket or cloth for scents
dietNotes: Chew only if your dog already eats it safely; skip it and use a blanket scent instead if you prefer.
safety: Approach where they can see or smell you, and never startle or touch a dog from behind.
Keep scents mild (no essential oils or candles) and the route clear of steps, with mats flat on non-slip underlay.
